passages.text: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will show compassion to Jacob.
The LORD will choose Israel again.
The LORD will settle Israel in their own land.
Foreigners will join Israel.
Foreigners will unite with the house of Jacob.
passages.original: כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם עַל־ אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנִסְפְּח֖וּ עַל־ בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland. Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
passages.sermon:
The nations will escort Israel.
The nations will bring Israel to its homeland.
The house of Israel will possess the nations in the land of the LORD.
The house of Israel will have the nations as menservants and maidservants.
Israel will make captives of those who once captured them.
Israel will rule over those who once oppressed them.
passages.original: וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ וֶהֱבִיא֣וּם אֶל־ מְקוֹמָם֒ וְהִֽתְנַחֲל֣וּם בֵּֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָח֑וֹת וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: On the day that the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the hard labor into which you were forced, you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will give you rest.
He will free you from your pain.
He will end your torment.
He will rescue you from the hard labor you were forced to do.
On that day, you will speak against the king of Babylon.
You will say this song about him.
The oppressor has stopped.
His violence has ended.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ וּמִן־ הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַקָּשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד־ בָּֽךְ׃ וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃

passages.text: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD acts with power.
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked.
The LORD has broken the scepter of the rulers.
The wicked used their staff to oppress.
The rulers used their scepter to rule harshly.
The LORD ended their power.
passages.original: שָׁבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה מַטֵּ֣ה רְשָׁעִ֑ים שֵׁ֖בֶט מֹשְׁלִֽים׃

passages.text: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon struck many peoples.
He struck them with great anger.
He did not stop striking them.
He ruled over nations with rage.
He persecuted them without showing mercy.
passages.original: מַכֶּ֤ה עַמִּים֙ בְּעֶבְרָ֔ה מַכַּ֖ת בִּלְתִּ֣י סָרָ֑ה רֹדֶ֤ה בָאַף֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם מֻרְדָּ֖ף בְּלִ֥י חָשָֽׂךְ׃

passages.text: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.
passages.sermon:
God has acted.
God has brought peace.
Now the whole earth is quiet.
The whole earth is at rest.
People everywhere rejoice.
They sing with joy.
passages.original: נָ֥חָה שָׁקְטָ֖ה כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ פָּצְח֖וּ רִנָּֽה׃

passages.text: Even the cypresses and cedars of Lebanon exult over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.”
passages.sermon:
The cypresses rejoice over you.
The cedars of Lebanon also rejoice over you.
You have been laid low.
Since you fell, no woodcutter comes against us.
passages.original: גַּם־ בְּרוֹשִׁ֛ים שָׂמְח֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַרְזֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן מֵאָ֣ז שָׁכַ֔בְתָּ לֹֽא־ יַעֲלֶ֥ה הַכֹּרֵ֖ת עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Sheol beneath is eager to meet you upon your arrival. It stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you— all the rulers of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
passages.sermon:
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Sheol lies beneath the earth.
Sheol becomes restless when you arrive.
Sheol is eager to meet you.
Sheol stirs up the spirits of the dead.
These spirits are the rulers of the earth.
Sheol makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
These kings stand up to greet you.
passages.original: שְׁא֗וֹל מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בּוֹאֶ֑ךָ עוֹרֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־ עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְאוֹתָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are; you have become like us!”
passages.sermon:
All the kings of the nations will speak to you.
They will answer you directly.
They will say these words to you.
You have become weak.
You are weak like us.
You have become like us.
passages.original: כֻּלָּ֣ם יַֽעֲנ֔וּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ גַּם־ אַתָּ֛ה חֻלֵּ֥יתָ כָמ֖וֹנוּ אֵלֵ֥ינוּ נִמְשָֽׁלְתָּ׃

passages.text: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed and worms your blanket.
passages.sermon:
You were proud and exalted.
Now your pride has fallen down to Sheol, the place of the dead.
The music of your harps has also gone down with you.
Maggots now cover the place where you lie.
Worms are your blanket.
passages.original: הוּרַ֥ד שְׁא֛וֹל גְּאוֹנֶ֖ךָ הֶמְיַ֣ת נְבָלֶ֑יךָ תַּחְתֶּ֙יךָ֙ יֻצַּ֣ע רִמָּ֔ה וּמְכַסֶּ֖יךָ תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃

passages.text: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the king of Babylon.
The king of Babylon was proud and powerful.
Isaiah calls him "day star, son of the dawn."
You have fallen from heaven.
You once stood high and strong.
Now you are cut down to the ground.
You destroyed many nations.
Now you are brought low.
passages.original: אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־ שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־ גּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks about a proud ruler.
This ruler thinks highly of himself.
He says these things in his heart.
He says, “I will go up to the heavens.
I will put my throne above the stars of God.
I will sit on the mountain where God’s people gather.
I will sit in the far north.”
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ בִֽלְבָבְךָ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֶֽעֱלֶ֔ה מִמַּ֥עַל לְכֽוֹכְבֵי־ אֵ֖ל אָרִ֣ים כִּסְאִ֑י וְאֵשֵׁ֥ב בְּהַר־ מוֹעֵ֖ד בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפֽוֹן׃

passages.text: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is the day star, son of the dawn.
The day star says, "I will ascend above the tops of the clouds."
The day star says, "I will make myself like the Most High."
passages.original: אֶעֱלֶ֖ה עַל־ בָּ֣מֳתֵי עָ֑ב אֶדַּמֶּ֖ה לְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.
passages.sermon:
You tried to rise high.
You wanted to be above all.
But you will fall down.
You will go to Sheol.
You will reach the lowest depths of the Pit.
passages.original: אַ֧ךְ אֶל־ שְׁא֛וֹל תּוּרָ֖ד אֶל־ יַרְכְּתֵי־ בֽוֹר׃

passages.text: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble, who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
passages.sermon:
People will see you.
They will look closely at you.
They will think about what happened to you.
They will ask, “Is this the man who shook the earth?
Is this the man who made kingdoms tremble?
He turned the world into a desert.
He destroyed its cities.
He did not let his captives go home.”
passages.original: רֹאֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יַשְׁגִּ֔יחוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ יִתְבּוֹנָ֑נוּ הֲזֶ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ מַרְגִּ֣יז הָאָ֔רֶץ מַרְעִ֖ישׁ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃ שָׂ֥ם תֵּבֵ֛ל כַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעָרָ֣יו הָרָ֑ס אֲסִירָ֖יו לֹא־ פָ֥תַח בָּֽיְתָה׃

passages.text: All the kings of the nations lie in state, each in his own tomb.
passages.sermon: All the kings of the nations die.\r\nEach king receives honor after death.\r\nEach king lies in his own tomb.
passages.original: כָּל־ מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם שָׁכְב֥וּ בְכָב֖וֹד אִ֥ישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.
passages.sermon:
You are not honored in death.
You are thrown out of your grave.
You are like a branch that people reject.
You are covered with the bodies of those killed by the sword.
You lie among those who go down to the stones of the pit.
You are like a dead body that people trample underfoot.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֞ה הָשְׁלַ֤כְתָּ מִֽקִּבְרְךָ֙ כְּנֵ֣צֶר נִתְעָ֔ב לְב֥וּשׁ הֲרֻגִ֖ים מְטֹ֣עֲנֵי חָ֑רֶב יוֹרְדֵ֥י אֶל־ אַבְנֵי־ ב֖וֹר כְּפֶ֥גֶר מוּבָֽס׃

passages.text: You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land and slaughtered your own people. The offspring of the wicked will never again be mentioned.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to a wicked king of Babylon.
You will not be buried with the other kings.
You destroyed your own land.
You killed your own people.
People will never mention the children of the wicked again.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תֵחַ֤ד אִתָּם֙ בִּקְבוּרָ֔ה כִּֽי־ אַרְצְךָ֥ שִׁחַ֖תָּ עַמְּךָ֣ הָרָ֑גְתָּ לֹֽא־ יִקָּרֵ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֶ֥רַע מְרֵעִֽים׃

passages.text: Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the sons of the wicked.
God commands people to prepare a place to slaughter these sons.
The sons must die because of the sins of their fathers.
These sons will not rise up.
They will not inherit any land.
They will not fill the earth with their cities.
passages.original: הָכִ֧ינוּ לְבָנָ֛יו מַטְבֵּ֖חַ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתָ֑ם בַּל־ יָקֻ֙מוּ֙ וְיָ֣רְשׁוּ אָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵֽי־ תֵבֵ֖ל עָרִֽים׃

passages.text: “I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her posterity,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is powerful and commands armies.
The LORD of Hosts says, "I will rise up against them."
The LORD of Hosts will act with authority.
The LORD of Hosts says, "I will cut off Babylon."
Babylon will lose her name.
Babylon will lose her remnant.
Babylon will lose her offspring.
Babylon will lose her posterity.
The LORD of Hosts declares this.
passages.original: וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאָ֛ר וְנִ֥ין וָנֶ֖כֶד נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He will act with power and authority.
He will make Babylon a home for owls.
He will turn Babylon into swamplands.
He will sweep Babylon away with the broom of destruction.
The LORD of Hosts declares this.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֛יהָ לְמוֹרַ֥שׁ קִפֹּ֖ד וְאַגְמֵי־ מָ֑יִם וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֙יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts has sworn: “Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
The LORD of Hosts has great power.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn an oath.
He says, “What I have planned will happen.
What I have decided will take place.
No one can stop My purpose.”
passages.original: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־ לֹ֞א כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּמִּ֙יתִי֙ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֔תָה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָעַ֖צְתִּי הִ֥יא תָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD rules over all armies.
The LORD says, “I will break Assyria in My land.
I will defeat Assyria on My mountain.
I will remove Assyria’s yoke from My people.
I will take away Assyria’s burden from their shoulders.”
passages.original: לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י וְעַל־ הָרַ֖י אֲבוּסֶ֑נּוּ וְסָ֤ר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ עֻלּ֔וֹ וְסֻ֨בֳּל֔וֹ מֵעַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖וֹ יָסֽוּר׃

passages.text: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts made a plan.
This plan covers the whole earth.
The LORD of Hosts stretched out His hand.
His hand reaches over all the nations.
passages.original: זֹ֛את הָעֵצָ֥ה הַיְּעוּצָ֖ה עַל־ כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזֹ֛את הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה עַל־ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God has made a plan.
No one can stop God’s plan.
God has stretched out His hand.
No one can turn God’s hand back.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יָעָ֖ץ וּמִ֣י יָפֵ֑ר וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃פ

passages.text: In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden was received: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.
passages.sermon:
King Ahaz died in that year.
God gave this message at that time.
Philistines, do not rejoice.
Do not be glad, all of you.
The rod that struck you is broken.
But do not think you are safe.
A viper will come from the root of the snake.
A flying serpent will come from its egg.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת־ מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃ אַֽל־ תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֙שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ כִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַכֵּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ מִשֹּׁ֤רֶשׁ נָחָשׁ֙ יֵ֣צֵא צֶ֔פַע וּפִרְי֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ף מְעוֹפֵֽף׃

passages.text: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the Philistines.
He says what will happen after their oppressor is broken.
The firstborn of the poor will find pasture.
The needy will lie down in safety.
I will kill your root by famine.
Your remnant will be slain.
passages.original: וְרָעוּ֙ בְּכוֹרֵ֣י דַלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לָבֶ֣טַח יִרְבָּ֑צוּ וְהֵמַתִּ֤י בָֽרָעָב֙ שָׁרְשֵׁ֔ךְ וּשְׁאֵרִיתֵ֖ךְ יַהֲרֹֽג׃

passages.text: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the Philistines.
He warns them after King Ahaz of Judah dies.
He says, “Gate, wail!”
He says, “City, cry out!”
He says, “All you Philistines, melt away!”
He explains why.
He says, “A cloud of smoke comes from the north.”
He says, “Its army has no stragglers.”
He means the coming army is strong and united.
He means the Philistines will face destruction.
passages.original: הֵילִ֤ילִֽי שַׁ֙עַר֙ זַֽעֲקִי־ עִ֔יר נָמ֖וֹג פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת כֻּלֵּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מִצָּפוֹן֙ עָשָׁ֣ן בָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין בּוֹדֵ֖ד בְּמוֹעָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? “The LORD has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD has founded Zion.
Zion is a city.
The LORD is God.
God made Zion strong.
God protects Zion.
God’s afflicted people are in need.
God’s afflicted people belong to Him.
God’s afflicted people will find refuge in Zion.
God will keep them safe there.
When envoys from a nation ask for an answer, this is the answer.
God has established Zion as a place of safety for His people in trouble.
